description: Team Epsilion is a focused, high-impact two-person engineering and space-research team from Dushanbe, Tajikistan Sino Nazarov and Khushvakhtov Muhammadjon.While larger teams divide tasks across dozens of roles, our tight-knit collaboration allowed us to move rapidly from NASA scientific research to a fully functional, multi-module deep-space medical prototype within the hackathon window.
summary: ASTRA HEALTH is an integrated astronaut health monitoring suite built for long-duration spaceflight. Addressing the 5 hazards of human spaceflight and communication delays in deep space, the platform combines real-time biometric telemetry, 3D anatomical risk mapping (targeting SANS and bone density loss), neutron radiation monitoring, mental health tracking, and autonomous AI-assisted medical triage. Designed for Earth, ISS, Lunar, and Martian environments, ASTRA HEALTH helps crews detect health anomalies early and maintain mission readiness far from Earth. Understand Your Body. Protect Your Mission.
details:
Our team built ASTRA HEALTH from scratch to solve a real problem: how astronauts can monitor their health and handle medical emergencies during deep-space missions when Earth is millions of kilometers away and communication takes up to 22 minutes.

  1. Researching Space Risks: We started by studying NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) data on the 5 main hazards of spaceflight—microgravity, radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, and closed habitats.
  2. Designing the Architecture: We structured the software into 5 clean Python modules (app.py, engine.py, database.py, visuals.py, and config.py) so the system works completely offline without relying on external cloud servers.
  3. Building the Simulation & Database: Using Python, NumPy, and SQLite, we created a physiological simulation engine that models vital signs, bone density loss, and neutron radiation spikes (inspired by NASA's CANS research) across Earth, ISS, Moon, and Mars environments.
  4. Creating the Interface: We used Streamlit and Plotly to build a Mission Control dashboard featuring a 3D interactive human body map (highlighting SANS and skeletal risks), live health trend charts, a mental health tracker, medical inventory, and an autonomous AI triage assistant that gives instant emergency protocols during solar flares.
dataRefs: NASA HRP: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
